breakthrough.summary: Vandier's own lexical index resolves the two genital nouns at XVI,16. The female-genital noun is kꜣ.t 'vagin'; the male-organ noun is ḥnn 'phallus' (two occurrences). The same index assigns the XVI,16 mḥ occurrence the gloss 's'emparer de (m)'.
breakthrough.consequence: The previously open cross-text identity of the female noun is now PASS: pJumilhac XVI,16 and pBrooklyn XI,11 both use kꜣ.t. The male-organ noun is not conserved: Jumilhac uses ḥnn whereas pBrooklyn's relevant phallus term is mṯꜣ.

female_genital.source_location: Vandier Index I, printed p.321 / scan p-315

male_organ.source_location: Vandier Index I, printed p.306 / scan p-300

retention_operator.source_location: Vandier Index I, printed p.294 / scan p-289
retention_operator.critical_note: Vandier note 545 additionally states mḥ n = mḥ m and considers, but disfavors, šd m 'retirer de'.
retention_operator.later_philological_control: Leitz 1994 argues for mḥ 'fill', with possible contextual 'swell', explaining the canid copulatory tie and retention.

semantic_sequence: mḥ: retention/seizing/filling-swelling operator at this locus
the phallus remains in the vagina

comparison_with_pbrooklyn.interpretive_result: kꜣ.t is now the more stable lexical anchor across the two traditions, while the phallus term varies. This materially strengthens corpus searches centered on kꜣ.t rather than on a single male-organ noun.

retention_semantics.vandier_note_545: mḥ n = mḥ m; alternative šd m 'retirer de' considered but first hypothesis preferred
retention_semantics.quack_translation_lineage: phallus held fast in the woman's vagina so that it cannot be taken out
retention_semantics.synthesis: The operator is securely mḥ. Its locus-specific semantic field combines seizure/retention with the filling-swelling interpretation developed in later philology. Do not collapse these into a modern mechanical clamp.

withdrawal_clause.semantic: Baba is unable to take/pull the phallus out
withdrawal_clause.warning: Do not promote the normalization to canonical exact transcription until sign-level verification is complete.

topa_template_upgrade.dedupe_rule: Shared translations or descendants of Vandier/Derchain/Leitz count as one evidence lineage unless an independent manuscript or lexical witness is present.

canonical_conclusion: pJumilhac XVI,16 securely uses kꜣ.t for the female vagina and ḥnn for the phallus (twice), with mḥ as the retention operator. This establishes an exact Egyptian lexical-mechanical template kꜣ.t + ḥnn + mḥ associated with inability to withdraw. Because pBrooklyn XI,11 independently uses kꜣ.t for a metallic vagina/vulva, the shared kꜣ.t lexeme across the two traditions is now proven. The male-organ lexeme differs, and no source yet proves that the Mendes metallic kꜣ.t physically enclosed, clamped, or received the Osirian phallus.
